title: Finite presentations over continuous field coefficients on a noetherian base
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] with noetherian underlying topological space (every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes). Use the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] and the coefficient ring $E_X^c=p_X^*C(-,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. There is a canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism $E_X^c\cong (V\mapsto C(|V|,E))$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, where $V$ is a pro-etale site object and $|V|$ has its Zariski topology; the right side has pointwise operations and restrictions by composition. If an $E_X^c$-module sheaf $P$ has a pro-etale covering $\{V_\alpha\to X\}$ on which it is the cokernel of a map $(E_{V_\alpha}^c)^{m_\alpha}\to(E_{V_\alpha}^c)^{n_\alpha}$ with finite nonnegative $m_\alpha,n_\alpha$, then it has a pro-etale covering $\{W_\beta\to X\}$ on which $P|_{W_\beta}\cong(E_{W_\beta}^c)^{r_\beta}$ for finite nonnegative integers $r_\beta$. In particular this assertion applies to each noetherian locally closed stratum of a module sheaf constructible in the stratified local-finite-presentation sense of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], with strata as in [def-constructible-stratification]. No completeness condition on $P$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, sheaf-property proof; Stacks openness tool is the statement of the cited node

proof.text: Construct the adjoint by composing each continuous test function with the canonical projection |X[S]| → S. Prove projection naturality and ring compatibility, then transpose through the existing monoidal adjunction. On an affine U, use the explicit component-map equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-point-components-maps] to construct U → X[π₀(U)] and prove it terminal in the opposite comma category. Its Kan cocone leg is invertible. The comparison on U is composition with U → π₀(U); connected-component factorization and total disconnectedness of the finite normed extension E make this map bijective. On a weakly contractible affine, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-sheafification-wcontractible-sections] identifies the sheafification unit as invertible. Uniqueness of left adjoints transfers the Kan comparison to the given composite inverse image. The affine covers of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family] make the resulting sheaf morphism locally bijective, hence invertible. The adjoint equations on all test functions imply uniqueness by injectivity of the adjunction equivalence.

source.place: Example 3.1; restriction and basis-gluing argument written out

proof.text: Define $r(x)$ intrinsically, rather than from a chosen presentation. For a geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, pull back $P$ and then evaluate at $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The abelian inverse image preserves cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]; the composition comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] identify its coefficient ring with $E_{\operatorname{Spec}K}^c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-field-proetale-evaluation], evaluation preserves cokernels and has coefficient ring $C(*,E)=E$. Base changing a presentation covering to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ gives a covering there, and its section through one member lets one pull that finite presentation back to the final object. Consequently the evaluated module is a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space; set $r(x)$ equal to its dimension. Its value is independent of the algebraically closed representative: each such field contains an algebraic closure of $\kappa(x)$, and the extension comparisons of the same cited node preserve evaluation. In particular, if $v\in V_\alpha$ lies above $x$ and $A_\alpha$ is the $n_\alpha$ by $m_\alpha$ matrix of the presentation, then $r(x)=n_\alpha-\operatorname{rank}_E A_\alpha(v)$. A module map between finite free ring sheaves is a matrix of global ring sections: its columns are the images of the unit basis sections, and linearity determines it. The coefficient identification of the preceding step turns these sections into continuous functions.

source.place: Example 4.2.11; agent rank construction using exact inverse image and split covers, not the lisse-heart theorem

proof.text: If $x$ is a generalization of $y$ in $X$, choose $v\in V_\alpha$ above $y$. The map $V_\alpha\to X$ is flat by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Apply [lem-sc-flat-going-down] to the flat local ring map $\mathcal O_{X,y}\to\mathcal O_{V_\alpha,v}$, lifting the prime corresponding to $x$ below the maximal ideal; it gives a generalization $v'$ of $v$ above $x$. Continuous maps to the Hausdorff field $E$ have equal values at two comparable points: continuity carries specialization to specialization and a Hausdorff space has only equality specializations. Hence every entry of $A_\alpha(v')$ equals the corresponding entry of $A_\alpha(v)$. The formula of the preceding step proves $r(x)=r(y)$. No openness of the weakly etale covering map is assumed.

source.place: Agent rank descent; going-down source is Stacks Algebra Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), as recorded in the cited node

proof.text: The topologically noetherian hypothesis gives finitely many irreducible components $Z_i$ by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. Each has a generic point $\eta_i$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Every $x\in Z_i$ specializes from $\eta_i$, so the preceding step gives $r(x)=r(\eta_i)$. Therefore each rank level is a union of some of the finitely many closed components. Its complement is also a finite union of closed components, so the level is clopen. These finitely many clopen levels cover $X$. Notice that algebraic noetherianity of coordinate rings was not used.

source.place: Agent topological rank argument; finite-components and sobriety tools are Stacks Tags 0052 and 01IS, respectively

proof.text: Restrict each presentation on $V_\alpha$ to the inverse images of the clopen rank levels of $X$. These are open subschemes and cover $V_\alpha$. Restriction preserves its cokernel by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] identifies the restricted coefficient with the corresponding coefficient ring sheaf. On one such piece $V$, write its matrix as $A$, of size $n$ by $m$, and write $r$ for the base rank. The evaluation formula from step 3 gives $\operatorname{rank}_E A(v)=s:=n-r$ at every point $v\in V$. In particular $0\le s\le\min(m,n)$.

source.place: Agent argument: pull back the rank partition, retaining each original finite presentation

proof.text: For $s>0$, the nonvanishing loci of the $s$ by $s$ minors of $A$ are open and cover $V$; for $s=0$ use all of $V$. On a locus with invertible minor, permute rows and columns to write $A=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}B&C\cr D&H\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with $\det B\ne0$ everywhere. The entries of $B^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(B)/\det B$ are continuous, so define ring sections on this locus. The invertible block operations give $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}B^{-1}&0\cr -DB^{-1}&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)A\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-B^{-1}C\cr 0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\cr 0&H-DB^{-1}C\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Pointwise rank $s$ implies every entry of the Schur complement vanishes at every point; since these sections are actual functions, it is the zero matrix of sections. The cokernel is thus the free coefficient sheaf of rank $n-s=r$. If $s=0$, every entry of $A$ vanishes pointwise and its cokernel is the free sheaf of rank $n$. This proves a sheaf isomorphism by explicit matrix operations, without using geometric-point conservativity.

proof.text: The opens in step 7 cover each piece in step 6, and those pieces cover the given presentation covering. Composing gives the required pro-etale finite-free covering; this local-freeness theorem remains the single open Lean obligation. The application to strata is proved: restriction gives a module over the pulled-back coefficient ring. Transport it along the inverse of the canonical condensed coefficient pullback isomorphism. Additive finite-colimit-preserving functors carrying the regular module to the regular module preserve finite presentations, by their finite-biproduct and cokernel comparison isomorphisms. This proves preservation of local finite presentations under the coefficient isomorphism. Apply the local-freeness theorem to the stratum, transport its free modules back using finite-biproduct comparisons, and use naturality of mapModComapIso to obtain exactly the displayed restricted modules. No nonempty, positive-rank, or positive-presentation-size assumption is used.
